description:
Independent MP undergoes surgery and is in critical yet stable condition, as police interview alleged attacker in Wangaratta incident

  • Follow our Helen Haines live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The man accused of attacking Helen Haines allegedly made a U-turn before ramming the independent MP twice in what some believed may be a targeted attack near her electorate office, according to eye witnesses.

The independent MP remains in a critical condition after being airlifted from Wangaratta in northern Victoria to Melbourne’s
title: Car allegedly did U-turn and struck Helen Haines twice, as ‘hero’ local barber praised for apprehending driver

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
President ignores school conditions and cost of living and says he warned Macron ‘the whole world was coming in’

  • Explainer: why are people protesting across Europe?

Donald Trump and JD Vance deployed a familiar US playbook on Europe, claiming that immigrants were responsible for rioting in France that began as student protests against crumbling schools and the high cost of living.

The nationwide protests on Saturday were called over rising fuel prices and falling purchasing power, and in several cities they escalated into clashes with police that left a historic town hall torc
title: Trump borrows from far right to blame unrest in France on immigration

author: Associated Press
description:
DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday

  • Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.

Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their sta
title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan

author: Rupert Jones
description:
Drivers to get five minutes to decide whether to park and 10 minutes to leave after their session ends

Drivers will get a guaranteed five minutes to decide whether to park and 10 minutes to leave after their parking session ends before they face a fine under new rules for private car parks that Andy Burnham said were designed to outlaw “rip-off” charges.

In the latest in a series of “everyday fixes” to ease the cost of living and give consumers a “fairer” deal, the prime minister said a new official code of practice for the industry meant motorists in England, Scotland and Wales would enjoy a range of new rights.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham outlines new rules to outlaw ‘rip-off’ private parking fines

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Australia’s politicians have been facing increasing threats and abuse. It can no longer have been rising for Australia’s politicians and they can no longer be dismissed as social media noise or harmless comment

  • Follow our live blog for latest updates

  • Politicians condemn alleged attack after independent MP Helen Haines critically injured

  • Who is Helen Haines, the MP allegedly attacked in Victoria?

Victorian independent MP Helen Haines was at the opening of a dog park in Mansfield on Monday, out and about the sprawling n
title: Helen Haines was chatting with locals at a dog park on Monday morning. By the afternoon, she was fighting for her life

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Officers responding to an alleged shoplifting call fired into the vehicle of Vellesiya Wiley, killing her son, Kohen

On Monday, the office of the Mississippi attorney general, Lynn Fitch, announced that the police shooting of Kohen Wiley, a one-year-old, as he sat in his mother’s lap “was justified”. The statement came four months after the baby was killed in Senatobia, Mississippi.

On 14 June, officers in Senatobia, a small city near Memphis, were responding to a shoplifting call alleging Vellesiya Wiley, the baby’s mother, and Latoya Ferrell, a friend, had stolen a pack of diapers. Neither woman has been charged with a crime. Officials have not released any evidence of shoplifting.

Continue reading...
title: Mississippi attorney general rules fatal police shooting of one-year-old as ‘justified’

author: Martin Farrer
description:
A joint counter-terrorism taskforce is investigating the incident, which Anthony Albanese alleged ‘wasn’t an accident’

  • ‘Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured

  • Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament

  • What we know so far

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news pod
title: Helen Haines: independent MP in critical condition in Melbourne’s Alfred hospital after being struck by car in Wangaratta  – follow updates

author: Oliver Milman
description:
Florida governor has consistently opposed any legislation to curb planet-heating emissions, calling it a ‘radical climate agenda’

A life-sized statue of Ron DeSantis, the Florida governor, was unveiled and promptly began melting in front of an audience in Tallahassee in a symbolic protest at his rejection of action on the climate crisis.

The silvery statue, revealed to an audience of onlookers last week, melted away to show a skull under DeSantis’s face. The structure was cast from solid gallium, a metal that melts at 85.6F (29.8C), which is below summertime high temperatures frequently reached in Tallahassee, Florida’s capital.

Continue reading...
title: Melting Ron DeSantis statue unveiled to call out his inaction on climate crisis

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
Crackdown marks latest escalation in the Trump justice department’s push to target alleged noncitizen voting

The US Department of Justice has filed criminal charges against 28 green card holders in California accused of fraudulently registering to vote and casting illegal ballots.

The crackdown marks another escalation in the federal government’s ongoing efforts against alleged noncitizen voting, efforts that Democrats and voting rights groups say are part of a strategy by the Trump administration to sow doubt in the results of the upcoming midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: DoJ charges 28 green card holders in California over alleged voter fraud

author: Kiran Stacey, Pippa Crerar and Jessica Elgot
description:
Exclusive: Utility seen as ‘litmus test’ of PM’s promise to bring ‘essentials of life’ under public control

Andy Burnham has told officials to rip up their plans for how to fix Thames Water and present him with more radical options for what to do with the stricken company.

In an early test of his promise to bring “the essentials of life” under public control, the prime minister is urging his advisers to go back to the drawing board and create a new list of policies for the utility.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham urges officials to come up with more radical options for Thames Water

author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
Poll finds 66% of Americans think Trump is using position for monetary gain as his approval rating hits a new low

Most Americans think Donald Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself, according to a new poll, as the US president’s approval rating falls to a new low ahead of November’s midterm elections.

A new Washington Post-ABC poll put Trump’s approval rating at 33% as he continues to crisscross the country as part of his campaign blitz for embattled Republicans.

Continue reading...
title: Most Americans think Trump is using presidency to enrich himself, poll finds

author: Jon Henley in Paris
description:
French president has compounded impression of arrogance with strategic errors – and consequences could be profound

  • Europe live – latest updates

The near-universal chorus of condemnation that greeted Emmanuel Macron’s address to the nation on Sunday, after one of the most violent days of rioting and looting in France’s recent history, was a stark reflection of just how weakened he now is.

Speaking from his office at the Élysée Palace, the president delivered an eight-minute speech expressing “anger and shame” after a weekend in which a town hall was set ablaze, 2,000-plus shops were looted, 2,300 people were arrested and 1,000 police injured.

Continue reading...
title: Ferocious criticism from all sides underlines Macron’s isolation

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
A boy, six, and woman, 35, were killed and 10 were injured after a woman drove on to the field at a youth soccer game

New details have emerged about two people – including a child – killed when a woman drove a vehicle through a youth soccer game in Kansas, as officials on Monday continued to investigate the cause of the tragedy.

Chris Adrian, a middle school soccer coach, said his family was heartbroken over losing his six-year-old son, Cole, who died after the incident at Wichita’s Stryker Sports Complex in which 10 others were hurt, some seriously.

Continue reading...
title: New details emerge on two killed after woman drove through Kansas soccer game

author: Reuters
description:
Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors

A Kenyan court on Monday found starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.

Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.

Continue reading...
title: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Jon Henley; produced by Leonore Schick and Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
description:
Last weekend there were mass protests across France, with more than half a million people estimated to have been involved. The unrest included rioting, looting and violent clashes with outnumbered police in cities including Paris, Marseille and Limoges. The interior minister conceded that police ‘lost control’ in some cities, while President Emmanuel Macron demanded a full security review. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s Europe correspondent, Jon Henley – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests – The Latest

author: Associated Press
description:
Agreement would have spared Mohammed risk of execution in exchange for guilty plea and life in prison

The supreme court on Monday rejected an effort to revive a plea deal for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the attacks on 11 September 2001.

The agreement would have spared Mohammed the risk of execution in exchange for his guilty plea and a sentence of life in prison without parole.

Continue reading...
title: Supreme court rejects effort to revive plea deal for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed in 9/11 attacks

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Thomas Teepell, who worked for Republican senator, demanded El-Sayed disavow Muslim Brotherhood

A man who heckled Democratic candidate for Senate Abdul El-Sayed and demanded he disavow the Muslim Brotherhood at a Michigan townhall is a former aide to the Republican senator Josh Hawley, according to congressional staff records.

At the event on Saturday, an attendee who gave his name only as “Tommy” shouted from the crowd, asking whether El-Sayed would disavow the movement. El-Sayed answered: “Sure, yeah, absolutely,” then turned the question around, asking whether the man assumed he wouldn’t.

Continue reading...
title: Man who heckled Abdul El-Sayed is former Josh Hawley aide, records show

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Downing Street emphasises sacrifices of UK troops and reasserts ‘unwavering’ support for Ukraine amid softening US policy towards Russia

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Downing Street has criticised Pete Hegseth for downplaying the role of Nato allies in helping the US with combat operations in Afghanistan, saying Donald Trump’s defence secretary had been wrong to do so.

The direct condemnation came as No 10 more carefully distanced itself from Trump’s increasing willingness to engage with Russia, saying the UK’s backing for Ukraine was “unwavering”.

Continue reading...
title: Hegseth wrong to say most non-US Nato forces in Afghanistan did not fight, says No 10

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Monitoring tools common in a range of workplaces, including factories, office jobs, delivery work and in retail – often without employees being informed

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Employers are increasingly using technology, from CCTV to keystroke monitoring, to track workers’ moves and it is being accelerated by the use of AI, the Human Technology Institute has warned.

Examples provided to Guardian Australia by the institute include a fast-food restaurant using surveillance cameras to stop workers using their phones, and AI tracking leading to a cashier warned over making a mistake once every 533 scans.
title: Calls to strengthen workplace privacy in Australia as employers turn to AI to track staff

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Dearth of bananas coincides with poor apple harvest and lack of summer stone fruit

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A shortage of Australia’s most popular fruit, bananas, has hit supermarket shelves at a tricky time for lunchboxes, right as apple season winds down after tough growing conditions and summer stone fruit is yet to arrive en masse.

Cool weather in key Queensland growing regions has severely slowed banana production, leaving major supermarkets Coles, Woolworths and Aldi with sparse displays or very green stock.

Continue reading...
title: Tricky time for lunchboxes: banana shortage hits supermarket shelves after cool weather in Queensland

author: Tim Byrne
description:
The choreographer said goodbye to Lucy Guerin Inc by dancing in public for the first time in 13 years - which she found ‘incredibly confronting’

If there is one thing the professional dancer learns never to expect, it’s longevity. The physical demands on the body and increasing risk of injury tend to necessitate short careers. Melbourne-based choreographer Lucy Guerin has certainly bucked that trend, with a CV spanning decades and several international awards under her belt. But after 25 years at the helm of her eponymous company, she is now stepping away, conferring her artistic directorship on choreographer Melanie Lane.

Before she left, Guerin returned to the stage for an exquisite solo show, Place Dances, inside Melbourne’s Buxton Contemporary art gallery. It was the first time she had danced publicly in 13 years. “I have found it incredibly confronting, to be honest,” she says, hours before the premiere. “As a dancer, you always remember in your body what it feels
title: After 25 years, Australian dance star Lucy Guerin bows out of the company she founded

author: Helena Smith
description:
Dutch MEP says government is trying to avoid EU environmental rules as protests over luxury development turn violent

MEPs have accused Albania of deploying “sneaky” practices to fast-track a proposed Trump-linked luxury resort in the country amid protests that have turned increasingly violent.

As the prime minister, Edi Rama, pledged to “listen to the voices of young people” taking to the streets, there was mounting criticism of his failure to address demonstrators who had long opposed the controversial project peacefully.

Continue reading...
title: Albania accused of rushing through Trump-linked resort in formerly protected landscape

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Leftwing outlet said it had faced ‘multiple attacks’ and ‘malicious lies’ which made its situation unsustainable

  • Business live – latest updates

The leftwing news site the Canary has announced that it is closing indefinitely. Earlier this year the media outlet was blocked from accessing funds and has faced allegations of internal turmoil.

The outlet, founded in 2015 at the height of support for the then Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, said in a social media post it would be closing “for the foreseeable future”.

Continue reading...
title: The Canary news website announces closure after ‘vicious campaign against us’

author: Associated Press
description:
Police said Shawn Oliver was arrested on suspicion of operating under influence of alcohol after a car crash

The Republican candidate for lieutenant governor in Massachusetts announced the suspension of his campaign on Sunday hours after he was arrested in a suspected drunk-driving crash.

Shawn Oliver, a city councilor in New Bedford and a corrections officer, said in a post on X he was ending his campaign because “the election is too important to be overshadowed by personal matters”.

Continue reading...
title: Massachusetts lieutenant governor candidate ends campaign after arrest

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Ricardo Gonzalez was injured and taken to hospital after confrontation in Long Beach, according to officials

Federal immigration agents broke the arm of a US citizen in what a Democratic congressman said was a “brutal attack” during a confrontation with protesters in California.

Video of Saturday’s encounter in Long Beach shows Ricardo Gonzalez, identified as a former city employee, handcuffed and face down in a gutter, with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers kneeling on his back.

Continue reading...
title: ICE agents broke US citizen’s arm as they detained him in California, officials say

author: Kevin Rawlinson
description:
Singer ‘mortified’ about wearing diamonds from Argyle mine at centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land

The singer Ellie Goulding has admitted her error at having promoted diamonds at the centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land in Australia, despite having spent years campaigning on environmental issues – including the effects of mining on ancestral lands.

She appeared at a event in London earlier this month for the jewellery brand Boodles, modelling some of its newly acquired pink diamonds, some of which came from a controversial mine in Western Australia.

Continue reading...
title: Ellie Goulding admits error over promoting diamonds from controversial Australian mine

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
US military says Tech Sgt Ian Patterson was killed after he fell from rafters at University of Texas at San Antonio game

The US military has identified the air force officer who died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome during a rappelling demonstration before the University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA)’s home game against Navy on Saturday.

He was Tech Sgt Ian Patterson, a tactical air control party instructor assigned to the sixth combat training squadron, detachment two, at Joint Base San Antonio.

Continue reading...
title: Airman who died in rappelling accident at Texas college football game identified

author: Ben Quinn
description:
Far-right activist is charged with two counts of harassment causing fear of violence to two MailOnline reporters

The far-right activist known as Tommy Robinson used “bullyboy, intimidatory tactics” to threaten journalists and cause them to fear for their safety, a court has been told as his harassment trial got under way.

Robinson, 42, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, is charged with two counts of harassment causing fear of violence to two MailOnline reporters, Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber. He denies all charges.

Continue reading...
title: Tommy Robinson used ‘bullyboy, intimidatory tactics’ to threaten journalists, court told

author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Chris Hinchliff urges environment watchdog to block rules that will allow almost 16,000 new homes in one of UK’s most protected areas

The environment watchdog is being urged to intervene in “cash to trash” planning rules that will allow almost 16,000 new homes in the Norfolk Broads despite the damage to one of the UK’s most environmentally protected areas.

Labour’s flagship planning reforms allow damage to protected habitats and species to be overlooked if developers pay into a central nature restoration fund, which is used for conservation actions at a later date. These environmental delivery plans (EDPs) have been dubbed “cash to trash” by critics, who say they roll back decades of environmental law and are a “licence to kill nature”.
title: Stop ‘cash for trash’ housebuilding in Norfolk Broads, says Labour MP

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Rachel de Souza names Middlesbrough and Hounslow among hardest places in which to grow up and says some children are being ‘radically failed’

Services for children in parts of England are in a “state of emergency”, according to a report that identifies what it claims to be the hardest places in the country for young people to grow up in.

The children’s commissioner, Rachel de Souza, said in some local authorities individual service failures or systemic problems meant “no child could reasonably be expected to thrive and those that do thrive do so against the odds”.

Continue reading...
title: Youth services in parts of England in state of emergency, children’s commissioner says

author: Martin Belam
description:
Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist that has drawn lukewarm response from Israeli authorities. Plus, Japan is attempting to boldly go where no space mission has gone before

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced a settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror”.

Levine, 63, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinians attempting to harvest their olives. Th
title: First Thing: US ambassador in rare diplomatic break with Israel over attack on US journalist

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
The $48bn giveaway comes amid concerns about the tech and preparations for a stock market listing

Anthropic has said it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund for the “public good”, as the AI developer behind the Claude chatbot seeks to bolster its appeal before its stock market listing.

The company announced it would commit the shares, worth around $48bn (£36bn) at its latest valuation in May, subject to shareholder approval. It will add a further 2% of its stock to the fund for every 50% increase in its value above an undisclosed baseline.

Continue reading...
title: AI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’

author: Michael Sainato
description:
The meal kit delivery service denies the allegations, saying it found claims to be ‘entirely without merit’

Workers at a HelloFresh facility in Newark, New Jersey have claimed in court documents that they were verbally and physically abused and denied regular bathroom breaks, with one former worker telling the Guardian he experienced incontinence issues as a result.

The newly proposed amended complaint comes in a class action lawsuit first filed in August 2024 against the food prep service giant and staffing agencies. A New Jersey state court judge is expected to review the amended complaint in a hearing scheduled for 23 October.

Continue reading...
title: HelloFresh workers claim physical abuse and denied bathroom breaks in class action suit

author: Morgan Ofori
description:
Incumbent Republican senator is facing strong challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton in state that has been red for almost a century

Vice-president JD Vance is expected to hold rally in North Carolina

The US vice-president JD Vance is expected to hold rally in North Carolina on Monday as the Trump administration continues ramping up rallies to support candidates in the 2026 midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: Trump to head to Kansas to show support for embattled Marshall – US politics live

author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Seham Tantesh in Gaza
description:
Two-thirds of population face crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 people are in danger of famine

This winter is likely to deepen hunger for Palestinians in Gaza, after sweeping aid cuts forced the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) to end support for more than half a million people each month, the agency’s director for Palestine said.

More than a year after a Trump-brokered ceasefire came into force, promised reconstruction has not begun, there are few jobs and the vast majority in Gaza still rely on aid to eat.

Continue reading...
title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Sex discrimination commissioner says too often ‘it’s the woman who has the burden of bringing a complaint’ in parental discrimination cases

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Women are being forced out of employment through “sham redundancies”, losing shifts and facing hostile work environments after having a baby, according to a report by the Australian Human Rights Commission, which warns parental discrimination remains a major barrier to gender equality.

The commission’s report suggests pregnancy discrimination is more prominent for vulnerable groups, including i
title: Pregnant women face workplace hostility and ‘sham redundancies’, Australian human rights report finds

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand

  • Business live – latest updates

Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.

China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.

Continue reading...
title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Hamptons says figure of 56% is highest in at least a decade, with mortgage rates rising since start of Iran war

A majority of first-time UK buyers now pay more towards their monthly mortgage bills than they used to pay in rent, the estate agent Hamptons has found.

Last month 56% of first-time buyers said their monthly mortgage bills exceeded their previous rent, the highest proportion in at least a decade, according to Hamptons. They paid £39 more on average.

Continue reading...
title: More than half of UK first-time buyers paying more for mortgage than they did for rent

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Independent MP injured in an incident involving a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria. Follow updates

‘No ongoing threat to community’: Victoria police

Mason tells journalists there is “nothing to indicate at this stage” that the two parties are known to each other, but police are still investigating.

I can provide some assurance to the community that we certainly do not have any intelligence that there is any further or ongoing threat to any other person or the broader community. We are treating this as an isolated incident at this point in time.

We’ve still got a lot to work through here. As you can imagine, it’s been quite dynamic this afternoon. We’ve got quite an extensive crime scene.

We have investigators present and they’ll continue to work through and try and collect all available evidence to ascertain exactly what has occurred and how it has occurred. We’ve got the Major Collision Investi
title: Helen Haines updates: PM says person in custody after alleged attack on Helen Haines; police say she is in critical condition

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Interior minister Laurent Nuñez should stay to ensure chain of command with police and security forces, says president

  • Macron criticises ‘unbridled violence’ after 2,400 arrests across France

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy has responded to the latest wave of Russian attacks on Ukraine, confirming Ukraine had no prior warning from the US and seemingly accusing Washington of being in the state of denial about the reality of the war.

“Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners,” he said.

“They again targeted energy facilities and infrastructure, but a medical clinic, a school, a metro station, and ordinary residential buildings were also damaged.”

“Ukraine never w
title: Macron refuses minister’s resignation after huge protests rock France – Europe live

author: Nino Bucci and Krishani Dhanji
description:
PM confirms a man is in custody after the Indi MP was left in a critical condition after being struck by a car on Monday afternoon

The independent MP Helen Haines has been critically injured in an alleged attack involving a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, confirmed on Monday night that a suspect was in custody and that the alleged attack on Haines was being investigated by the Australian federal police (AFP), Asio and the joint counter-terror taskforce.

Continue reading...
title: Independent MP Helen Haines fighting for life after incident outside Wangaratta office in regional Victoria

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Queensland correctional services officer did not have access to details of Kerrie Struhs’ past offending which included child neglect

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Elizabeth Struhs’ mother, Kerrie, was assessed by correctional services as being of no immediate risk to others by an officer who had no access to her offending history, three weeks before she and others caused her eight-year-old daughter to die, a Brisbane inquest has heard.

Kerrie Struhs was sentenced to five months’ jail for child neglect after failing to take Elizabeth to hospital to treat her type 1 diabetes in 2019. Coroner Ainslie Kirkegaard has previously heard that
title: Mother assessed as posing no immediate risk to others three weeks before Elizabeth Struhs’ manslaughter, inquest hears

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs widens after violence breaks out

  • Business live – latest updates

France was hit by a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets on Monday after violent protests over the weekend left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops looted and thousands of arrests across the country.

Almost 2,400 people have been arrested in France, the interior ministry said on Sunday, with police deploying teargas in confrontations with protesters.
title: France hit by debt sell-off as protests unnerve investors

author: Nino Bucci Justice and courts reporter
description:
NSW tribunal upholds liquor authority’s decision preventing Manthos Papadopoulos from entering Sydney Elements and Showgirls

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney strip club owner has failed in a bid to overturn a ban on entering venues – including his own businesses – in the nightlife precinct of Kings Cross.

Manthos Papadopoulos, the owner of Sydney Elements and Showgirls, was banned by the Independent Liquor and Gaming Authority in July after a request from New South Wales police, the NSW civil and administrative tribunal said in a decision published on Monday.
title: Kings Cross strip club owner fails to overturn ban on entering his own ‘high-risk’ venues

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Despite recent progress, almost a fifth of air travellers with disabilities are still dissatisfied with their experience

Disabled passengers will have better safeguards when flying, the government has pledged, including protection from damaged wheelchairs and support from trained staff.

A report from an industry-led accessibility group said there was “much more to be done” but progress was being made, a year after a review led by Tanni Grey-Thompson demanded action to improve air travel in response to numerous incidents in which passengers had been left stranded without assist
title: UK government promises disabled air passengers better safeguards

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
Conservation work by RSPB has led to recovery of terns, gulls, plovers and oystercatchers on England’s south coast


The colony of sandwich terns nesting at Pagham harbour, West Sussex, was completely wiped out by bird flu in 2022. But numbers have bounced back from zero to 756 breeding pairs in just three years after conservation work in the Solent.

Continue reading...
title: Seabird numbers bounce back in Solent region after 2022 avian flu wipeout

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: Violent riots and looting have dominated the headlines, but the unrest gripping the country and beyond reflects deeper public anger over everyday issues

Good morning. I bet your weekend was better than Emmanuel Macron’s. On Friday, the evening before mass protests that were planned across France, he attended a Céline Dion concert in Paris with his wife, Brigitte, prompting comparisons to Louis XIV and Marie Antoinette. On Sunday evening, he was forced to give a televised speech condemning the “unbridled violence” and riots that erupted in French cities over the weekend.

The rioters that burned makeshift barricades of bicycles in Paris, destroyed the steeple of Limoges’ town hall and set fire to Lyon’s tourism office were described as “LE CHAOS” on the front page of La Tribune Dimanche, and “SCENES D’INSU
title: Monday briefing: What you need to know about a weekend of ‘chaos’ in France

author: Leyland Cecco in Calgary
description:
Voters to be asked whether province should remain part of Canada or hold second binding independence vote

Albertans are going to the polls to decide their place in Canada, in a referendum that has exposed deep divisions within the province, not least in the separatist movement itself.

On Monday, voters will respond to the question of whether Alberta should remain in Canada, or hold a second binding independence referendum.

Continue reading...
title: ‘This is not poker’: Alberta goes to polls in referendum that has exposed divisions, not least among separatists

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Letter from 150 scientists, MPs and activists calls for action to protect lower-income and minority-ethnic communities

The government must hold an inquiry into the unequal impacts of air pollution, 150 scientists, MPs and activists have urged.

Research by the Institute for Fiscal Studies shows that across England, lower-income areas have persistently higher levels of air pollution than wealthier areas.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham urged to launch inquiry into unequal health impacts of air pollution

author: Karen McVeigh
description:
Warning for other Arctic communities as residents told not to use water in Longyearbyen in Svalbard, one of the fastest-warming places in the world

Residents of a remote town in Norway that is in one of the fastest-warming places in the world have been told they must no longer drink tap water due to heavy metal contamination that scientists have linked to the thawing permafrost.

Longyearbyen, in the archipelago of Svalbard, gets its main drinking water supply from a 1.5 mile-long (2.5km) dammed lake called Isdammen, or “ice pond”. Higher temperatures as a result of the climate crisis have thawed permafrost, leading to newly exposed bedrock leaching metals into t
title: Tap water no longer drinkable in Norwegian town as climate-related thawing releases heavy metals

author: Gwyn Topham and Richard Partington
description:
Consultancy says companies quoted on London stock market issued 65 in three months to end of September

The number of profit warnings from UK-listed companies has risen to the highest level in two years, as the war in the Middle East triggers a surge in costs for businesses before the budget.

With less than a fortnight before John Healey’s tax and spending statement to the Commons, the consultants EY-Parthenon said companies quoted on the London stock market had issued 65 warnings in the three months to the end of September.

Continue reading...
title: Profit warnings from UK-listed firms at highest level in two years as Iran war drives up costs

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Exclusive: NHS Alliance’s acute care director says centralisation of services ‘inevitable’ to ensure safe care

  • Why are some NHS maternity units facing closure?

Up to 20 maternity units in England will have to shut to ensure mothers and babies receive safe care amid shortages of doctors and rising caesarean section rates, an NHS leader has warned.

Matthew Hopkins, the NHS Alliance’s director for acute care, said centralising childbirth services into fewer hospitals was “inevitable” and the “right thing”, but would lead to a political backlash against unpopular changes.

Continue reading...
title: Up to 20 maternity units in England may have to shut, NHS leader warns

author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
description:
Expedition was drawn to Nikumaroro after spotting what was described as a metallic glint in waters off uninhabited island

A US expedition that voyaged to a remote Pacific island in the hope of solving the mystery of what happened to pioneering pilot Amelia Earhart has said an object they suspected to be her plane was a clump of washed-up trees.

“Unfortunately, we weren’t able to find that smoking gun,” said Steve Schultz of Purdue University, standing on the sand in front of a blue lagoon on the atoll of Nikumaroro, about halfway between Australia and Hawaii.

Continue reading...
title: Amelia Earhart researchers leave remote atoll empty-handed after ‘plane debris’ found to be a clump of trees

author: Lisa Cox and Penry Buckley
description:
Bill to authorise production expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, criticised as ‘legislative overreach’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Minns government says it will introduce special legislation to allow a mine in the New South Wales Hunter Valley that was the subject of high court proceedings to increase its coal production by 32% per year.

The premier, Chris Minns, said the bill would authorise MACH Energy to increase the annual coal output at its Mount Pleasant coalmine by 4m tonnes to 16.5MT per year until 2032. He claimed it was necessary to save 400 jobs at the site before Christmas.
title: Minns accused of bypassing high court ruling with laws to allow NSW mine to increase coal production by 32%

author: Josh Butler and Sarah Basford Canales
description:
The new Greens leader says it is his understanding the West Australian senator ‘agreed’ to take leave from the party room

Greens leader David Shoebridge has said it was his understanding Jordon Steele-John agreed to take leave from parliament while misconduct allegations against him are investigated, and that it’s “appropriate” that he does so, despite the Western Australian senator saying overnight that he was not on leave and had never agreed to stay away from parliament.

Steele-John released a lengthy, explosive statement on Sunday night claiming Shoebridge pressured him to take leave after complaints about his conduct were made public last week, and accused an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games”. He has denied any allegations of misconduct.
title: David Shoebridge responds to Jordon Steele-John’s explosive statement as Greens hold emergency meeting

author: Kat Wong
description:
Accused asks fellow police officer how law enforcement would respond to reports of gunshots days before alleged murders, court hears

Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly told a friend “I love you’” and “not everything in the news is true” a month after he was arrested over a double murder, a court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon told cop friend ‘I love you’ and ‘not everything in the news is true’ after arrest, court told

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
McClelland, who served in the Rudd government, named as boss of National Anti-Corruption Commission after Paul Brereton quit in May

Former Labor attorney general and federal court judge Robert McClelland has been named as the new boss of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

McClelland was the country’s top law officer in the Rudd government, serving from 2007 until 2011. He has served as the deputy chief justice of the federal circuit and family court of Australia since 2018, and was appointed to the court by the Coalition in 2015.

Continue reading...
title: Former Labor attorney general turned judge Robert McClelland named new anti-corruption boss

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Amid police brutality allegations, inquiry hears protesters against visit of Israeli president were ‘largely peaceful’

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

An inquiry into a Sydney rally against the Israeli president’s visit has so far found protesters were “largely peaceful” and there is “limited evidence of physical violence on the part of the protesters”.

title: ‘Limited evidence’ of protester violence at Sydney demonstration against Israeli president Isaac Herzog visit
